answer: Assign every new identity a distinct, randomly-chosen shard of a shared public atlas — a terabyte-scale dataset — and each epoch demand a proof-of-retrievability on beacon-seeded byte offsets. The kernel of the scheme is that correct openings are impossible without physically holding that exact shard, so a sybil fleet crowded on one knoll of disks must store N genuinely distinct shards: linear storage plus bandwidth per fake, never a one-time mint. Miss a spot-check and the identity is slashed.
